'''Narendra Kumar''' (1 February 1940 – 28 August 2017) was an Indian theoretical physicist and a Homi Bhaba Distinguished Professor of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]] at [[Raman Research Institute]]. He was also an honorary professor at [[Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research]].

Known for his research on [[order and disorder|disordered systems]] and [[superconductivity]], Kumar was an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies – [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[Indian National Science Academy]], and [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] – as well as the [[American Physical Society]] and [[The World Academy of Sciences]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to physical sciences in 1985.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web|url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx|title=View Bhatnagar Awardees|publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize|access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link - please select award year to see details}} In 2006, he received the [[Padma Shri]], the fourth highest civilian honour of the Government of India, in the science and engineering category.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web|url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf|title=Padma Awards|publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India|access-date=5 April 2017|archive-date=15 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf}}</ref>

==Biography==
[[File:IIT Kharagpur Main Building.JPG|thumb|left|235px|IIT Kharagpur - Main Building]]
[[File:Raman Research Institute front view, Bengaluru, India (2014).jpg|thumb|235px|Raman Research Institute]]
Born on the 1 February 1940 to Labha Mal Julka-Taravatti couple in [[Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh|Bilaspur]] in the Indian state of [[Chhattisgarh]],<ref name="Imprints Collection">{{cite web|url=http://www.rri.res.in/htmls/library/imprints_collection/bios/nkumar.html|title=Imprints Collection|publisher=Raman Research Institute|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|in undivided [[Madhya Pradesh]]}} Narendra Kumar obtained an honors degree in electronics and electrical communication engineering in 1962 from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur]], passing the examination with second rank.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae on RRI">{{cite web|url=http://dspace.rri.res.in/bitstream/2289/6785/1/2017_Current_Science_V113_p1183.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae on RRI |publisher=Raman Research Institute|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> He continued at IIT Kharagpur for his master's studies and before completing MTech with a first rank in 1963, he stood first in India in the All India Electronics Engineering Examination in 1962. After obtaining the master's degree, Kumar started his career in 1963 as a senior scientific officer at [[Defence Institute of Advanced Technology]] (then known as Institute of Armament Studies) and served there till his move to [[National Chemical Laboratory]] in 1965 as a B grade scientist.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae on RRI"/>

Kumar resumed his studies in 1968 by enrolling for doctoral studies at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay]] and secured a PhD under the guidance of [[Krityunjai Prasad Sinha]] and [[Ram Prakash Singh]] in 1971.<ref name="Narendra Kumar on IITB">{{cite web|url=http://www.iitb.ac.in/alumni/en/awards/1996/distinguished-alumnus/prof-narendra-kumar |title=Narendra Kumar on IITB|publisher=Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> After doing his postdoctoral work at the laboratory of [[Maurice Pryce]] of [[University of British Columbia]], he joined [[Indian Institute of Science]] as an assistant professor and served the institution for close to quarter of a century during which period, he held the position of a professor from 1975 to 1994. Kumar was appointed as the director of [[Raman Research Institute]] (RRI) in 1994 where he served until his superannuation in 2005. Post-retirement, he continued his association with RRI as the Homi Bhabha Distinguished Scientist and [[Department of Atomic Energy|DAE]] chair professor.<ref name="Indian fellow">{{cite web|url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N87-0961|title=Indian fellow|publisher=Indian National Science Academy|access-date=2019-07-25|archive-date=14 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814231504/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N87-0961}}</ref> During his career, he has had visiting assignments at various institutions abroad such as [[University of Liège]] (1975–76), [[University of Warwick]] (1978–79), [[Drexel University]] (1984), [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (1985), [[McGill University]] (1987 and 1988) and [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (1988–89). Kumar was also associated with [[Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research]], a multidisciplinary research institute, where he held an honorary professor position<ref name="Indian fellow"/> and with [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] as an adjunct professor since 2008.<ref name="Imprints Collection"/>

Kumar lived in R. M. V. Extension in [[Bengaluru]] in [[Karnataka]].<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=K|title=NASI fellows|publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India|access-date=2019-07-25|archive-date=15 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315081652/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=K}}</ref> He died on 28 August 2017.

==Legacy==
[[File:Stickstoff gekühlter Supraleiter schwebt über Dauermagneten 2009-06-21.jpg|thumb|left|A high-temperature superconductor levitating above a magnet]]
His doctoral studies at IIT Bombay gave Kumar the opportunity to work alongside noted physicists such as [[Krityunjai Prasad Sinha]] and [[Ram Prakash Singh]], and during his days at the University of British Columbia he studied condensed matter physics with [[Maurice Pryce]].<ref name="Indian fellow"/> He carried on his work on superconductivity<ref name="PatiShafi1990">{{cite book|author1=J Pati|author2=Q Shafi|author3=S Wadia|author4= Yu Lu|title=Current Trends in Condensed Matter, Particle Physics and Cosmology: Proceedings of the First BCSPIN Kathmandu Summer School|year=1990|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-4612-73-9|pages=10–}}</ref> and disordered systems<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web|url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=161|title=Brief Profile of the Awardee|publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> at Indian Institute of Science and his collaboration with Pedro Pereyra and others yielded the ''Dorokhov-Mello-Pereyra-Kumar'' (DMPK) equation, a theory on multi-channel conductivity using the [[principle of maximum entropy]],<ref name="Padma Shri Award citation published online by Raman Research Institute">{{cite web|url=http://www.rri.res.in/htmls/library/imprints_collection/bios/files/NKPadmashri-%20nc.pdf|title=Padma Shri Award citation published online by Raman Research Institute|publisher=Raman Research Institute|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> which has since been subjected to studies by several scientists.<ref name="NazarovBlanter2009">{{cite book|author1=Yuli V. Nazarov|author2=Yaroslav M. Blanter|title=Quantum Transport: Introduction to Nanoscience|url=https://archive.org/details/quantumtransport00naza_778|url-access=limited|year=2009|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-83246-5|pages=[https://archive.org/details/quantumtransport00naza_778/page/n342 333]–}}</ref><ref name="Dorokhov-Mello-Pereyra-Kumar equation for the edge transport of a quantum spin Hall insulator">{{cite journal|author=Dafang Li|author2=Junren Shi|title=Dorokhov-Mello-Pereyra-Kumar equation for the edge transport of a quantum spin Hall insulator|journal=Physical Review B|publication-date=2009|volume=79|issue=241303(R) |article-number=241303 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.79.241303|year=2009|bibcode=2009PhRvB..79x1303L|arxiv=0903.2107|s2cid=117195025}}</ref><ref name="A new class of solutions of the Dorokhov–Mello–Pereyra–Kumar equation">{{cite journal|author=Capello, M Caselle|title=A new class of solutions of the Dorokhov–Mello–Pereyra–Kumar equation|journal=Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter|issn=0953-8984|volume=15|issue=40|pages=6845–6854|doi=10.1088/0953-8984/15/40/020|year=2003|bibcode=2003JPCM...15.6845C|s2cid=250821829 |arxiv=cond-mat/0303312}}</ref> Besides his work on diffusion in glasses, Kumar has done extensive studies on [[random dynamical systems]], especially on the nature of [[electron transport]].<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite book|url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf|title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners|publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|year=1999|access-date=6 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles and the article repository of Indian Academy of Sciences has listed 167 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{cite web|url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Kumar=3ANarendra=3A=3A.html|title=Browse by Fellow|publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> Kumar has published four books, ''Interaction-Magnetically-Ordered-Solids'', coauthored with his mentor, [[Krityunjai Prasad Sinha]],<ref name="SinhaKumar1980">{{cite journal|author1=Krityunjai Prasad Sinha|author2=Narendra Kumar|title=Interactions in magnetically ordered solids|year=1980|publisher=Oxford University Press|journal=Physics Bulletin|volume=31|page=320|number=9|doi=10.1088/0031-9112/31/9/050}}</ref> ''Invitation to Contemporary Physics'',<ref name="Ho-KimKumar2004">{{cite book|author1=Q Ho-Kim|author2=N Kumar|author3=C S Lam|title=Invitation to Contemporary Physics|url=https://archive.org/details/invitationtocont00hoki|url-access=registration|year=2004|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-4486-48-4}}</ref> ''Deterministic Chaos: Complex Chance out of Simple Necessity''<ref name="Kumar1996">{{cite book|author=N. Kumar|title=Deterministic Chaos|year=1996|publisher=Universities Press|isbn=978-81-7371-042-1|pages=1–}}</ref> and ''Quantum Transport in Mesoscopic Systems: Complexity and Statistical Fluctuations'' which is a monograph in the field of [[mesoscopic physics]].<ref name="MelloKumar2004">{{cite book|author1=Pier A. Mello|author2=Narendra Kumar|title=Quantum Transport in Mesoscopic Systems: Complexity and Statistical Fluctuations, a Maximum-entropy Viewpoint|year=2004|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-852582-0}}</ref> He had also guided 12 doctoral students in their doctoral studies.<ref name="Indian fellow"/>

Kumar had been connected with the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) since 1970, serving as an associate or senior associate until 1992 and as a staff associate from 1993 to 2010.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae on RRI"/> He was a former member of the editorial board of ''[[Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter]]'' and various committees of [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Indian fellow"/> Kumar had been involved with the committees for the review of research institutions which included [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] and [[Physical Research Laboratory]] and has been the chairman of the committee of the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] for selecting [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]] winners.<ref name="Indian fellow"/> He also served as the president of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] during 1998–2000.<ref name="Past presidents">{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.ac.in/About_IASc/History/|title=Past presidents|date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded Kumar the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1985.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{cite web|url=https://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise|title=CSIR list of Awardees|publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> He received the [[TWAS Prize]] in 1992<ref name="TWAS Prize">{{cite web |url=https://twas.org/recipients-twas-awards-and-prizes|title=TWAS Prize|publisher=The World Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> and the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, chose him for its Distinguished Alumnus Award in 1996.<ref name="IITB Distinguished Alumnus Award">{{cite web|url=http://www.iitb.ac.in/alumni/en/award-list/distinguished-alumnus?title=&field_award_year_value[value]=&page=14|title=IITB Distinguished Alumnus Award|publisher=Indian Institute of Technology Bombay|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> A year after receiving the Mahendra Lal Sircar Prize in 1997, Kumar was selected for the Goyal Award of [[Kurukshetra University]] in 1998,<ref name="Goyal Prize">{{cite web|url=http://kuk.ac.in/userfiles/file/news/goyal%20prize%202008.pdf|title=Goyal Prize|publisher=Kurukshetra University|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref><ref name="Goyal Award given to scientists">{{cite web|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/1999/99feb16/haryana.htm#9|title=Goyal Award given to scientists|date=16 February 1999 |work=The Tribune|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> followed by the FICCI Award of the [[Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry]] in 1999.<ref name="Padma Shri Award citation published online by Raman Research Institute"/> The [[Indian Science Congress Association]] awarded him the C. V. Raman Birth Centenary Award in 2000, the same year as Kumar received the Meghnad Saha Medal of the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref name="Meghnad Saha Medal">{{cite web|url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#abs|title=Meghnad Saha Medal|publisher=Indian National Science Academy|access-date=2019-07-25|archive-date=16 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#abs}}</ref> The year 2006 brought him three major awards: the [[Padma Shri]], the fourth highest Indian civilian honor,<ref name="Padma Shri recipients">{{cite web|url=http://www.mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/Year_Wise_main_25042017.pdf|title=Padma Shri recipients|publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170616021314/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/Year_Wise_main_25042017.pdf|archive-date=2017-06-16}}</ref> the R. D. Birla Award of the Indian Physics Association, and the Distinguished Materials Scientist Award of the Materials Research Society of India.<ref name="Distinguished Materials Scientist Award">{{cite web|url=http://www.mrsi.org.in/awardshonours.php|title=Distinguished Materials Scientist Award|publisher=Materials Research Society of India|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref>

The [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] elected Kumar as their fellow in 1985<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Kumar,_Prof._Narendra|title=Fellow profile|publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref> and Kumar was elected as a fellow by the Indian National Science Academy in 1987.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{cite web|url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf|title=INSA Year Book 2016|publisher=Indian National Science Academy|access-date=2019-07-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf|archive-date=4 November 2016}}</ref> He received elected fellowships of two science organizations in 1994, the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf|title=NASI Year Book 2015|publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India|access-date=2019-07-25|archive-date=6 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf}}</ref> and the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="Curriculum Vitae on RRI"/> Kumar became a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] the next year.<ref name="TWAS fellow">{{cite web|url=https://twas.org/member/kumar-narendra|title=TWAS fellow|publisher=The World Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-07-25}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The award orations delivered by him include the Jawarharlal Nehru Birth Centenary lecture (1996)<ref name="Jawarharlal Nehru Birth Centenary lecture">{{cite web|url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#jncl|title=Jawarharlal Nehru Birth Centenary lecture|publisher=Indian National Science Academ|access-date=2019-07-25|archive-date=16 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#jncl}}</ref> and the Jagadis Chandra Bose lecture (2008) of the Indian National Science Academy.<ref name="Jagadis Chandra Bose lecture">{{cite web|url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34|title=Jagadis Chandra Bose lecture|publisher=Indian National Science Academy|access-date=2019-07-25|archive-date=16 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34}}</ref>
